titleEn: Stop and Look at the Crossing!

pages.text: "Dad, that older deer girl is lost!" Bami pointed across the railway crossing. A deer student with a schoolbag studied a map as yellow ginkgo leaves fell. "I'll bring her!" Bami was already hopping away.
Ding, ding, ding! The crossing bell rang. Without listening or looking left and right, Bami stepped forward. Dad followed and pinned the scarf's end with his foot. "Wait, Bami!"
The barrier lowered. A long, loaded freight train rattled past. Wind rushed over Bami, ruffling every feather. "A fright, wasn't it?" Dad asked. Bami's heart pounded.
Dad crouched to meet Bami's eyes. "At a crossing, our promises come before hurrying. Shall we make three?" Bami nodded. "How?"
Dad pointed at the barrier. "The crossing's wing! Down means stop, up means cross. And the bell says, 'Stop and look!'" Bami looked up at the arm. "Stop and look at the crossing?"
Dad explained clearly. "One, stop before the barrier! Two, look left and right for trains! Three, cross when the barrier rises!" Bami planted their feet. "I can do it! Stop and look!"
The barrier rose and the bell fell silent. Bami stopped, looked left, looked right, and crossed step by step. The deer student held out her map. "Little conductor, is this the station?"
"Yes! Let's cross together." Bami led her back, side by side. Stop, look, cross—onto the platform! Bami spread their wings. "I kept the promises myself!"
Now Bami kept them at every crossing. "One, stop before the barrier! Two, look left and right! Three, cross when it rises!" Boarding the train, the student repeated, "Stop and look at the crossing!"

The bell rang once. Before departure, Dad cuddled Bami with his wings. "Our promises won over hurrying!" However eager Bami felt, they stopped and looked before crossing. Stop and look at the crossing!
